title: Funky Drummer and Clyde Stubblefield
hook: 20 seconds of drums. No credit on the sleeve.
voiceover: 20 seconds of drums. No credit on the sleeve. November 1969, King Studios, Cincinnati. James Brown's band is cutting Funky Drummer. Late in the take, Brown tells everybody to lay out and lets Clyde Stubblefield play 8 bars alone. That's the break. Released in 1970 as a 2 part single, and Stubblefield's name isn't on it. Fight the Power. Mama Said Knock You Out. Run's House. George Michael's Waiting for That Day. Hundreds more. Stubblefield said in interviews he never got a royalty for any of it, because the record belonged to James Brown, not the drummer. I still cut those 8 bars in every hip-hop room I play. Name a record on Funky Drummer I missed.
caption: Funky Drummer, James Brown, recorded November 1969 at King Studios in Cincinnati, released 1970. The 8 bars Clyde Stubblefield plays alone are under Fight the Power, Mama Said Knock You Out, Run's House, George Michael, Sinead O'Connor and hundreds more. Stubblefield wasn't credited and, by his own account, never saw a royalty. Name a record on Funky Drummer I missed. 🥁
